findings.title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a P-256 key and never verify the converted DER signature
findings.body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default EC key pair (`KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which defaults to 256-bit P-256) in the constructor and reuses it across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Because the key is P-256, `signature.sign()` always produces ~70-72 byte signatures with 32-byte `r` and `s` components, even when signing with `SHA384withECDSA` or `SHA512withECDSA`. Consequently, 48-byte (P-384) and 66-byte (P-521, where ASN.1 lengths exceed 127 bytes and exercise multi-byte DER length encoding in `ASN1Encoder`/`ASN1Decoder`) `r`/`s` values are never tested. In addition, `test()` only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` -> `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` -> `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` round-trips to the same byte array; it never feeds `asn1Des` into `Signature.verify(...)` with the public key to confirm that `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` actually produces a valid ASN.1 DER signature accepted by the JCA provider.

findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` and discard both return values before lines 119-120 perform the exact same encoding inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements allocate `ByteArrayOutputStream` instances and encode `r` and `s` for no effect and should be removed.

findings.title: Unparameterized logger.debugf call with dynamic string can fail if provider name contains '%'
findings.body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a dynamically constructed string as the `printf` format pattern with no arguments. If any provider class name or representation ever contains `%`, `String.format` will throw `UnknownFormatConversionException`. Pass a format string (`logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` or use `logger.debug(builder.toString())`) instead.
